label: token right after an early "i" (orig position 1 or 2)
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at steps 2-3, on the token immediately following an "i" that was input at position 1 or 2 (99.7% of activation mass has prev_tok == i). Mostly position-specific: the rate falls off sharply at t=4 (i at position 3), where activations are weak, and there is nothing at t>=5, in the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The current token barely matters. The strongest activations come at t=3 with i at position 2 (e.g. q 2 i [l], q n i [m]); the first token q/e shows a mild lift. Weak at the lower end: some steps after i at t=3 stay inactive (around 8% false positives), and there are rare weak firings after the digit 2 or j.

issues: The core claims check out on dev and test. 99.7% of activation mass has prev_tok == i. Activations: t=2 61.6% of mass, t=3 37.4%, t=4 1.0% (weak), and zero at t=0, t=1 and t>=5. There are 0 copy-phase activations. Copying from an i in the copy phase gives F1 0.002.

Small overclaim on 'nothing in the delimiter': there are 43 delimiter activations on dev. They come from L=3 with i at position 2, where step 3 is the <DEL>. Dropping phase==0 from the predicate still gives F1 0.933 vs 0.938, so this is negligible.
Asymmetry between the two positions: t==2 alone has test precision 1.000. All false positives are at t==3, where precision is 0.838.

The t==3 false positives are systematic, not scattered. They depend on the two tokens before the i. With first_tok=m precision is 0.44, l 0.59, v 0.54, h/r 0.80, x 0.85, and q/e 1.00. With orig(1)=m it is 0.43, d 0.62, h 0.68, k 0.71, and 2/n 0.96. Calling this a 'mild lift' for q/e understates a roughly 2x modulation by history.
'Strongest at t=3' holds for peak activations (top examples are q 2 i [l]), but t=2 has more total mass (61% vs 37%).

I could not find a better simple predicate. Excluding the low-precision orig(0)/orig(1) tokens at t==3 raises test precision to 0.951 but lowers recall to 0.911, so F1 is 0.931, no gain over 0.938. The gap is a graded modulation by history, not a clean rule.
skeptic.revised_label: token right after an early "i" (orig position 1 or 2); at position 2 the firing is also modulated by the first two tokens

final_label: token right after an early "i" (orig position 1 or 2); at position 2 the firing is also modulated by the first two tokens
